unit.label: Gentle actions, appointments & clock time
unit.title: Making Plans by the Clock
unit.description: 11 new words and forms. Soften requests, make an appointment, tell exact time, and say when you are free.
unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 6, pp. 116–118; Lesson 7, pp. 130–145. Original examples and exercises.

lessons.title: Say It More Gently
lessons.subtitle: Finish this lesson with softened actions and corrective 不是.

steps.prompt: Which version makes the request sound lighter?
steps.explanation: Repeat the action verb itself: 幫幫. The object stays outside the repetition.

steps.prompt: Someone assumes you do not want to go. Which opening corrects that assumption?
steps.explanation: 不是不… means “it is not that I do not…”, and prepares a correction.

steps.prompt: You are correcting “You do not want to learn Chinese.” Which opening rejects that assumption?
steps.explanation: 不是 rejects the assumed negative claim; 不想 alone would confirm it.

lessons.title: Meet at KTV
lessons.subtitle: Sing, meet friends, and read Taiwan’s KTV shorthand.

steps.prompt: Which word means “to meet” in this lesson?
steps.explanation: 見面 means to meet; 唱歌 means to sing.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 唱 is chàng, the verb in 唱歌.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 見 is jiàn, the first character of 見面.

lessons.title: Meet at 9:20
lessons.subtitle: Read exact clock times with 點 and 分.

steps.prompt: What time is 九點二十分?
steps.explanation: 九點 gives the hour and 二十分 gives twenty minutes.

steps.prompt: In 九點, what does 點 mean here?
steps.explanation: The same written 點 has a clock-time use here.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 分 is fēn, minute in clock time.

steps.prompt: Your appointment is at 7:40. Which time matches?
steps.explanation: 七 is the hour, 四十 is forty minutes.

lessons.title: When and Where
lessons.subtitle: Put time before place and ask when something happens.

steps.prompt: Which word order is correct?
options: 我後天晚上在學校見面。
我在學校見面後天晚上。
steps.answer: 我後天晚上在學校見面。
steps.explanation: Time comes before place, and both come before the event.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 午 is wǔ, the noon character in 中午.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 時 is shí, the first character of 時候.

lessons.title: From Morning to Noon
lessons.subtitle: Frame a time range and say when you are free.

steps.prompt: In 從早上七點到中午, which word marks the starting point?
steps.explanation: 從 marks the start; 到 marks the endpoint.

steps.prompt: Which means “to be free / have available time”?
steps.explanation: 有空 literally has 空 and means to be free or available.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 從 is cóng, from.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 空 is kòng in 有空.

steps.prompt: 從中午到晚上 describes which range?
steps.explanation: 從 introduces the start, 中午; 到 introduces the end, 晚上.

lessons.title: Keep the Plan Moving
lessons.subtitle: Use next time, no problem, and by the way naturally.

steps.prompt: Which phrase means “next time”?
steps.explanation: 下次 refers to the next occasion.

steps.prompt: Which response means “No problem”?
steps.explanation: 沒問題 is the set response “No problem.”

steps.prompt: Which phrase is used like “By the way…” when remembering another point?
steps.explanation: 對了 can shift to a newly remembered topic.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 次 is cì, the occurrence counter in 下次.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 題 is tí, the second character of 問題.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 對 is duì, first character of 對了.

lessons.title: Unit 21 Review
lessons.subtitle: Appointments, clock time, ranges, and gentle corrections.

steps.prompt: Which sentence places time before place?
options: 我們後天晚上在學校見面。
我們在學校見面後天晚上。
steps.answer: 我們後天晚上在學校見面。
steps.explanation: Use Time → Place → Event.

steps.prompt: Which construction means “from A to B”?
steps.explanation: 從 marks the start and 到 the endpoint.

steps.prompt: Which sentence uses softened verb reduplication correctly?
steps.explanation: Repeat the action verb, not the verb-object phrase.

steps.prompt: Which opening means “It is not that I don’t want to go…”?
steps.explanation: 不是不… rejects the negative assumption.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 唱 is chàng.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 時 is shí.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 從 is cóng.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 題 is tí.

steps.prompt: Which keeps the meaning “We meet at school tomorrow evening”?
options: 我們明天晚上在學校見面。
我們明天晚上在餐廳見面。
我們後天晚上在學校見面。
steps.answer: 我們明天晚上在學校見面。
steps.explanation: Match both the time and the place: 明天晚上 is tomorrow evening; 學校 is school.

steps.prompt: Which time is 8:15?
steps.explanation: 十五 is fifteen; 五十 is fifty.

newVocabulary.meaning: to be free; have available time

唱.note: 唱 is the action verb in 唱歌, “to sing.” It is fourth-tone chàng.
唱.memory: A small 口 on the left faces a stacked 昌 on the right: picture a mouth producing song.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The three-stroke 口 sits tightly on the left and cues an action done with the mouth.

parts.label: 昌
parts.name: right sound block
parts.description: The right side is two 日-like boxes stacked vertically; keep both compact and aligned.

歌.note: 歌 is first-tone gē. In 唱歌, it names song while 唱 supplies the action.
歌.memory: The repeated square-and-hook shapes of 哥 stand beside 欠, whose final strokes open outward like a singer taking a breath.

parts.label: 哥
parts.name: left block
parts.description: The first ten strokes build the dense 哥 block on the left, with two 口-like sections and hooks.

parts.label: 欠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 欠 on the right, ending with the long right-falling stroke.

見.note: 見 is fourth-tone jiàn. In 見面 it contributes the idea of seeing or meeting someone.
見.memory: A five-stroke 目 eye stands above two 儿-like legs: an eye that goes out to see.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 目, a tall eye-shaped box with two inner horizontals.

parts.label: 儿
parts.name: lower legs
parts.description: The final two strokes spread below the eye; the last one bends and extends to the right.

分.note: 分 is first-tone fēn when it counts minutes in clock time, as in 二十分.
分.memory: 八 opens at the top over 刀 below; the four strokes divide the character into two clear parts.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: top split
parts.description: Two short spreading strokes form 八 at the top.

parts.label: 刀
parts.name: lower knife
parts.description: The last two strokes form 刀 underneath, with the second stroke sweeping down-left.

午.note: 午 is third-tone wǔ. In 中午 it refers to noon or midday.
午.memory: A short slant leads into two horizontals crossed by one vertical; keep the lower horizontal longer.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: top slant
parts.description: Begin with the short left-falling stroke at the upper left.

parts.label: 干
parts.name: two bars and a vertical
parts.description: The remaining three strokes form 干: two horizontal strokes followed by the vertical through them. This group has three strokes; it is not the two-stroke 十.

時.note: 時 is second-tone shí. It appears in 時候, a common way to talk about when something happens.
時.memory: 日 on the left is the sun/time cue; 寺 fills the right side with 土 above 寸.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The first four strokes make the narrow 日 on the left.

parts.label: 寺
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last six strokes form 寺 on the right, with a compact upper cross and 寸-like base.

候.note: 候 is fourth-tone hòu in 時候. The word 時候 is used in questions such as 什麼時候 “when.”
候.memory: A slim 亻 person stands at the left of a taller right block; keep the right side narrow enough to balance the person.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow person radical on the left.

parts.label: right block
parts.name: vertical and lower right block
parts.description: After 亻, the remaining eight strokes include a separate short vertical alongside the compact lower shape. This whole right group is not the complete character 侯.

從.note: 從 introduces the starting point of movement.
從.memory: Remember 從 by 彳 on the left and two person-like shapes above the spreading lower strokes on the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: step component
parts.description: 彳 is the narrow three-stroke component along the left edge.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right group
parts.description: The right group has two person-like shapes at the top and a long stroke extending toward the lower right.

空.note: 空 is fourth-tone kòng in 有空 (yǒu kòng), meaning to have time available. The audio uses 有空 to make this reading clear; 空 has other readings in other words.
空.memory: 穴 opens like a roofed space above 工: picture an empty space under a roof.

parts.label: 穴
parts.name: cave/space component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 穴, a roof with two small strokes opening underneath.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 工, centered under the upper space.

次.note: 次 is fourth-tone cì. In 下次 it means the next time or next occasion.
次.memory: Two small strokes on the left sit beside 欠 on the right; the final stroke of 欠 opens far to the right.

parts.label: 冫
parts.name: two-dot left side
parts.description: The first two strokes are a dot and rising stroke on the left.

parts.label: 欠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 欠, finishing with the long right-falling stroke.

題.note: 題 is second-tone tí. In 問題 it means a question or problem; 沒問題 means “no problem.”
題.memory: 是 fills the left side while the traditional 頁 head/page component forms the right side.

parts.label: 是
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first nine strokes form 是, beginning with 日 and ending in the sweeping lower strokes.

parts.label: 頁
parts.name: head/page component
parts.description: The last nine strokes form traditional 頁 on the right, with a boxed middle and two closing lower strokes.

對.note: 對 is fourth-tone duì. In 對了, it is a conversational cue meaning “by the way” or “oh, right.”
對.memory: A dense vertical left block balances 寸 on the lower right; keep the final dot of 寸 distinct.

parts.label: left block
parts.name: upper cluster and lower 土
parts.description: The first eleven strokes form the left block, including its upper cluster and lower 土-shaped base. The label describes the entire highlighted group, not just its upper portion.

parts.label: 寸
parts.name: right-lower component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 寸: a horizontal-hook structure followed by the small dot.

u21-softened-action.title: Soften an action with V-(一)-V
u21-softened-action.explanation: Repeating a mainly monosyllabic action verb presents the action as small, brief or tentative. In requests and suggestions it also makes the tone more moderate. When the verb has an object, repeat the verb, not the object: 看看書, not 看書看書.

examples.meaning: I want to read a little.

u21-softened-action.remember: Use this mainly with action verbs. V一V and VV have the same softening idea; do not reduplicate every verb automatically.

u21-not-the-case.title: Correct an assumption with 不是
u21-not-the-case.explanation: 不是 can reject a whole claim or assumption, not just identify a noun. It says “it is not the case that…”. It can even come before a negative clause: 不是不… means “it is not that I do not…”, usually before a correction or explanation.

examples.text: 他不是在樓下，他在二樓。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú shì zài lóuxià, tā zài èr lóu.
examples.meaning: It is not the case that he is downstairs; he is on the second floor.

examples.text: 我不是不想去，我今天要上課。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì bù xiǎng qù, wǒ jīntiān yào shàngkè.
examples.meaning: It is not that I do not want to go; I have class today.

u21-not-the-case.remember: Regular 不 negates a verb or state. 不是 here rejects what someone has said, assumed or contrasted.

u21-clock-time.title: Tell clock time with 點 and 分
u21-clock-time.explanation: Use 點 after the hour and 分 after minutes. The character 點 was learned earlier as “to order”; in clock time it is the measure for the hour. 分 here means minute. Put the hour before the minutes.
u21-clock-time.remember: Clock time is a time-when expression: 九點二十分, not 二十分九點.

u21-time-before-place.title: Put time before place
u21-time-before-place.explanation: When both time and place are stated, Chinese normally places the time before the place, and both come before the event. The subject may come before the time or immediately after it. Use the order Time + Place + Event.

examples.text: 我們後天晚上在學校見面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hòutiān wǎnshàng zài xuéxiào jiànmiàn.
examples.meaning: We will meet at school the evening after tomorrow.
I eat lunch at the restaurant at noon.

u21-time-before-place.remember: Think: WHEN → WHERE → WHAT HAPPENS. Do not put a time expression at the end just because English can.

u21-from-to-time.title: Mark a range with 從…到…
u21-from-to-time.explanation: 從 marks the starting point and 到 marks the endpoint. A and B may be times or places. In this unit, use the pattern especially to frame a time range, such as from morning to noon.

examples.text: 從早上七點到中午，我都有空。
examples.pinyin: Cóng zǎoshàng qī diǎn dào zhōngwǔ, wǒ dōu yǒu kòng.
examples.meaning: I am free from 7 in the morning until noon.

examples.pinyin: Cóng túshūguǎn dào sùshè bù yuǎn.
examples.meaning: It is not far from the library to the dorm.

u21-from-to-time.remember: 從 = start; 到 = end. Keep the two endpoints in their real order.

u21-soft-look.meaning: I want to read a little.
u21-soft-look.note: The repeated 看 makes the action feel light or brief.

u21-not-claim.text: 我不是不想去，我今天要上課。
u21-not-claim.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì bù xiǎng qù, wǒ jīntiān yào shàngkè.
u21-not-claim.meaning: It is not that I do not want to go; I have class today.
u21-not-claim.note: 不是不… rejects the assumption that the speaker does not want to go.

u21-ktv.note: KTV is the common Taiwan term for a karaoke venue; learn it here as a noun.

u21-meet.meaning: I will meet a friend the day after tomorrow.
u21-meet.note: 見面 is a separable verb meaning to meet.

u21-nine-twenty.pinyin: Wǒmen jiǔ diǎn èrshí fēn jiànmiàn.

u21-noon.meaning: I eat at the restaurant at noon.
u21-noon.note: 中午 is the time, so it comes before the place.

u21-time-place.text: 我們後天晚上在學校見面。
u21-time-place.pinyin: Wǒmen hòutiān wǎnshàng zài xuéxiào jiànmiàn.
u21-time-place.meaning: We will meet at school the evening after tomorrow.

u21-range.text: 從早上七點到中午，我都有空。
u21-range.pinyin: Cóng zǎoshàng qī diǎn dào zhōngwǔ, wǒ dōu yǒu kòng.
u21-range.meaning: I am free from 7 in the morning until noon.
u21-range.note: 從 introduces the start; 到 introduces the end.

u21-when-free.note: 什麼時候 is the standard beginner question for “when.”

u21-next-time.note: 下次 means the next occasion.

u21-no-problem.pinyin: Méi wèntí, wǒ hòutiān yǒu kòng.
u21-no-problem.meaning: No problem; I am free the day after tomorrow.
u21-no-problem.note: 沒問題 is a common response meaning “no problem.”

u21-by-way.pinyin: Duìle, nǐ shénme shíhou yǒu kòng?
u21-by-way.meaning: By the way, when are you free?
u21-by-way.note: 對了 shifts the conversation to something the speaker has just remembered.

u21-help-teach.note: 教教 softens the request; 我 remains outside the repeated verb.
